description: The image displays three pie charts, each representing the distribution of performance across different difficulty levels—labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard"—for a task related to geometric knowledge reasoning using large language models. Each chart is divided into three colored segments corresponding to different combinations of knowledge states: N+K+ (teal), N−K+ (light yellow), and N+K− (orange), with a legend provided on the right. In the "easy" category, the N+K+ segment accounts for 55.4%, the N−K+ segment for 38.3%, and the N+K− segment for 4.6%. In the "medium" category, the N+K+ segment is 58.8%, the N−K+ segment is 35.4%, and the N+K− segment is 4.0%. In the "hard" category, the N+K+ segment is 18.1%, the N−K+ segment is 37.3%, and the N+K− segment is 37.9%. The percentages are clearly labeled within each slice of the pie charts, and the segments are ordered in a clockwise direction, with the largest segment typically appearing first. The visual representation allows for a comparison of how the distribution of knowledge states changes with increasing difficulty.
